definitions.explanation: A person who accompanies one through life, typically a spouse or romantic partner. A somewhat formal or literary word that carries warmth and implies a deep, lasting bond.

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}の{伴侶|はんりょ}を{見|み}つけたい。
examples.english: I want to find a life partner.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{最良|さいりょう}の{伴侶|はんりょ}だと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: I think she is the best partner I could have.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{伴侶|はんりょ}を{亡|な}くし、{深|ふか}い{悲|かな}しみに{暮|く}れていた。
examples.english: Having lost a longtime partner, he was sunk in deep grief.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal, somewhat literary word most commonly seen in the phrase {人生|じんせい}の{伴侶|はんりょ} (life partner). More elevated than {配偶者|はいぐうしゃ} (which is bureaucratic) or パートナー (which is casual). Used in speeches, wedding contexts, and reflective writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人生|じんせい}の{伴侶|はんりょ} (life partner)
- {良|よ}き{伴侶|はんりょ} (good companion/partner)
- {伴侶|はんりょ}を{得|え}る (gain a partner)
- {旅|たび}の{伴侶|はんりょ} (traveling companion — literary)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {配偶者|はいぐうしゃ}: spouse — legal/bureaucratic term
- パートナー: partner — casual, modern term
- {連|つ}れ{合|あ}い: spouse — warm, colloquial term for husband/wife
